sweep.in_sweep_persistence_stamp: 5/20 sectors - fails persistence - blend-suspect (HIT line also flagged: high-contamination - blend risk)

odd_even.verdict_text: The two dips are different sizes — odd transits dip 0.004% but even transits dip -0.003% (159% apart). That is the classic sign of an eclipsing binary whose real period is twice the candidate period.

kill_reason: The app's ratio rule mechanically fired 'likely-eclipsing-binary' on a noise split of two zeros: odd/even folds +0.004% / -0.003% - no eclipse at either parity; deepest fold dip = 3.3% of the 0.120% BLS depth, far under the 25% evaporation line. Double-period agrees: no eclipse pair (0.048% / -0.008% at refined 22.266 d) and no ellipsoidal wave (+0.009% @ 1.6 sigma). Per the batch definition (cf. TIC 294671640, identical pattern) this is a PIPELINE PHANTOM; the raw app verdict is preserved as driver_verdict_raw.

double_period.verdict_text: The light between the eclipses is flat — quadratures sit at 1.0001 and the shoulders at 1.0000, a difference of +0.009% ± 0.006%, so there is no twin-star ellipsoidal wave. That is consistent with a real planet — or with a binary whose stars are too far apart to distort each other.
double_period.note: Post-gate diagnostic (driver gated at stage b); run to complete the brief's (a)-(c) fold set.

reclassification_note: Fold completion OVERTURNS the in-sweep stamp's blend reading. The stamp convicted on persistence (5/20) plus the HIT line's contamination flag (contratio 0.574, the dirtiest aperture of the sweep) - but the folds find no eclipse signal anywhere in the aperture, blended or on-target, at P or 2P. There is no neighbour EB to blame; what remains is a BLS-only signal on a sparse 42,957-point FFI star that evaporates in every fold. The contamination explains a noisy aperture, not this signal's mechanism.
